content:
Partition the board into sixteen \(2\times2\) blocks. In any \(2\times2\) block, every pair of squares is adjacent (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally), so at most one king can be placed in each block. Hence at most \(16\) kings.

This is attainable: place kings on all squares with odd row and odd column, e.g. \((1,1),(1,3),\dots,(7,7)\). These lie one per \(2\times2\) block and no two are adjacent.

\[
\boxed{16}
\]
